summary: Invoice subtotal/tax/total trusted from client, never recomputed
preconditions: An ADMIN session (or a finance:write df_ token bound to an admin) and at least one Client to invoice.
steps: Call finance.createInvoice (or POST /api/v1/invoices) with items:[{description:'Dev work',quantity:100,rate:150,amount:15000}] but subtotal:0, tax:0, total:0.
Observe the persisted invoice.
Open the finance summary / dashboard KPIs (totalPaid / totalOutstanding) and note the invoice contributes total=0.
Over REST, repeat with total:-15000 and observe paid/outstanding sums DECREASE.
expected: Server derives subtotal = sum(items.amount) and total = subtotal + tax (or rejects a mismatch); negative totals impossible.
actual: Inputs are written verbatim; total=0 stored while line items represent $15,000. There is no full invoice-EDIT mutation (only updateInvoiceStatus), so the wrong total is permanent and flows into totalPaid/totalOutstanding. Over REST a negative total decrements the books.
evidence: src/server/routers/finance.ts:201-214 writes subtotal: input.subtotal, tax: input.tax, total: input.total with no cross-field .refine. REST is worse: src/app/api/v1/invoices/route.ts:43-48 uses bare z.number() for subtotal/tax/total/amount (no .positive()). The AI tool does it correctly (recomputes with round2) at src/lib/ai/tools/finance.ts:482-490 — proving intended behavior.
fix: Recompute amount/subtotal/total server-side from items + tax in BOTH tRPC and REST; ignore client-sent totals (or .refine they match). Add a full invoice-edit path. (Verified first-hand.)

summary: Money aggregates sum USD + PKR into one $ figure
preconditions: Finance data containing more than one currency (USD and PKR). PKR is reachable via the AI assistant and REST createTransaction/createInvoice.
steps: Record June income of one USD transaction $5,000 and one PKR transaction Rs 280,000 (~$1,000).
Open the Finance KPIs and the Dashboard revenue tile.
expected: Aggregates group/convert by currency; mixed currencies are never summed into one scalar.
actual: transaction.aggregate({_sum:{amount}}) returns 285000; the finance KPI and dashboard render it through a hardcoded $ -> '$285,000'. True USD-equivalent ~ $6,000 — overstated ~47x.
evidence: No 'currency' appears in any aggregate where/groupBy. src/server/routers/finance.ts:332-353 (summary) and :389-396 (P&L); src/server/routers/dashboard.ts:48-59, :200-214; src/app/api/v1/finance/summary/route.ts; src/lib/ai/tools/finance.ts:122-138. UI renders hardcoded $: finance-content.tsx:92, dashboard-content.tsx:932.
fix: groupBy:['currency'] and report per-currency, or filter aggregates to a single currency, or convert via an FX table before summing. Never _sum a mixed-currency column into one scalar. (Verified first-hand.)

role: Any project member (e.g. EMPLOYEE on the project)
summary: Kanban drag-and-drop moves the wrong task when a filter is active
preconditions: A board with multiple tasks and at least one task that will be hidden by a filter.
steps: Open a board and apply any filter (search text, priority, assignee, or label) so >=1 task is hidden.
Drag a visible task to a new slot within or between columns.
Observe a DIFFERENT task is moved and a wrong order is persisted.
expected: The dragged task moves to the dropped slot.
actual: Rendered drag indices come from the FILTERED column list, but handleDragEnd splices into the UNFILTERED board.columns using those indices, so it removes/reinserts the wrong element and mutates with a wrong newOrder. With no filter active filteredColumns === board.columns so indices align and the bug is invisible — masking it in casual testing.
evidence: src/app/(app)/projects/[id]/board/[boardId]/kanban-board.tsx:164-189 — newColumns derived from board.columns, then sourceCol.tasks.splice(source.index,1) / destCol.tasks.splice(destination.index,0,...) use filtered indices; moveTask.mutate({ newOrder: destination.index }). Render uses filteredColumns (:372, Draggable index :483-484); filteredColumns returns board.columns only when !hasFilters (:233).
fix: Disable DnD while a filter is active, or translate the filtered source/destination indices back to real positions in board.columns (locate by draggableId) before splicing/mutating. (Verified first-hand.)

role: REST df_ token scoped clients:read, bound to an ADMIN user
summary: Full invoice/financial records reachable via a clients:read token
preconditions: A df_ token issued with only clients:read (no finance:read), bound to an admin user; a client that has invoices.
steps: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer df_<clients-read-token>' https://<host>/api/v1/clients/<clientId>
Observe every invoice for the client is returned (total/subtotal/tax/currency/status/dueDate/paidAt).
expected: A non-finance scope must not return financial data; even a wildcard * token cannot read finance data (the stated control).
actual: The route declares clients:read, so the admin finance double-gate never runs, and the handler returns every invoice for the client. The list route similarly leaks an invoice _count. Impact confined to admin-bound tokens (manual isAdmin gate), so a deliberately-narrow CRM integration token silently carries full finance read.
fix: Drop invoices from the clients:read include, or require hasScope(ctx,'finance:read') before including them.

summary: Revenue chart drops the last day of every month (+ month-overflow)
preconditions: An income transaction dated on the last day of a month, after midnight.
steps: Create an income transaction of $5,000 dated 2026-05-31 10:00.
Open the dashboard revenue chart and inspect the May bar.
Separately, view the chart on the 29th-31st of a month and compare month labels.
expected: The May 31 income is included in the May bar; month buckets are correct.
actual: endOfMonth = new Date(y, m+1, 0) is the last day at 00:00:00.000 and the query filters date: { lte: endOfMonth }, so anything after midnight on the final day is cut. The P&L report uses ...,0,23,59,59 and DOES include it, so chart and report disagree on every month's last day. Separately, date.setMonth(date.getMonth()-i) on today's day-of-month overflows on the 29th-31st (e.g. May 31 stepping back to 'Feb' rolls to Mar 3), duplicating/skipping a month.
fix: Build months with new Date(y, m-i, 1) and set endOfMonth = new Date(y, m+1, 0, 23, 59, 59, 999).

summary: This month/year KPIs have no upper date bound (future rows inflate)
preconditions: Ability to log a transaction with a future date (no max date validation).
steps: Log income of $1,000,000 dated 2030-01-01.
Open the Finance summary / Dashboard stats and view 'Monthly Revenue' and 'Net Profit'.
expected: Future-dated rows are excluded from this-month/this-year figures.
actual: The aggregates use date: { gte: startOfMonth } / { gte: startOfYear } with NO lte, so future rows are counted. The bounded P&L/chart then disagree with the KPI.
fix: Add lte: now (or end-of-period) to these aggregates.

summary: Recurring expenses excluded from P&L expense/profit
preconditions: RecurringExpense rows exist (seeded subscriptions ~$588/mo).
steps: View the P&L report / finance summary monthly expense and profit.
Compare against the recurring expenses list.
expected: Expense/profit include recurring costs.
actual: Every expense figure _sums the Transaction table only; RecurringExpense rows are never posted as transactions nor summed (getRecurringExpenses only lists them), so monthly burn/profit silently omit ~$588/mo and overstate profit.
evidence: src/server/routers/finance.ts:388-396, :419-423; recurring rows only read at :265-281.
fix: Materialize due recurring expenses as transactions on their due date, or add their per-period amount into expense/profit (currency-aware — see FIN-02).

summary: Invoice status: no transition guard, paidAt never cleared, double-notify
preconditions: An existing invoice.
steps: Mark an invoice PAID, then change it back to DRAFT.
Observe it stays DRAFT but keeps a paidAt timestamp.
Re-issue PAID on an already-paid invoice and observe paidAt overwritten and (AI path) a second invoice_paid activity + 'Payment received' notification/email.
expected: Illegal transitions blocked; paidAt/sentAt cleared when leaving PAID/SENT; side-effects idempotent.
actual: Any status -> any status; paidAt/sentAt set but never cleared; no priorStatus === status guard. OVERDUE is only computed at display time, so the stored status used by sums can be stale.
evidence: src/server/routers/finance.ts:236-238 (sets but never clears); AI src/lib/ai/tools/finance.ts:603-620 (unconditional notify on PAID). (Verified first-hand.)
fix: Validate allowed transitions; clear paidAt/sentAt on leaving; skip side-effects when status is unchanged.

summary: REST invoice/transaction money fields unvalidated (negatives & overflow -> 500)
preconditions: A finance:write df_ token bound to an admin.
steps: POST /api/v1/invoices with total: 99999999999999 -> numeric overflow against Decimal(12,2).
POST /api/v1/invoices with total: -500.
expected: A clean 400 and rejection of negatives.
actual: Bare z.number() (no .nonnegative()/.max()). Overflow -> unhandled DB exception -> generic 500; -500 is accepted and decrements paid/outstanding sums. The tRPC layer correctly uses nonNegativeMoney(); REST does not mirror it.
fix: Apply .nonnegative().max(MAX_MONEY) (and .multipleOf(0.01)) to all REST money fields.

role: Any employee (viewer); note authored by any user
summary: Activity feed leaks SHARED-note titles + cross-team activity to all staff
preconditions: Three users A, B, C. A creates a SHARED note shared only with B. C is neither recipient nor on the related project.
steps: As A, create a SHARED note titled 'Acme layoff plan' shared only with B.
As C, open /dashboard (or call dashboard.getRecentActivity).
Observe C sees: A created note 'Acme layoff plan' / A shared note '...' with 1 member.
expected: SHARED notes are visible only to author + recipients (enforced in notes.list/getById/search).
actual: The feed is filtered ONLY for finance event types — not by note visibility or project membership — so SHARED-note titles, plus task/project/client names from projects the viewer cannot access, are broadcast to all authenticated users. The developer comment intends 'team-visible' but the check is visibility !== 'PRIVATE', which INCLUDES SHARED.
evidence: src/server/routers/notes.ts:260-263 (logs title for any non-PRIVATE note), :385 (share activity with title); src/server/routers/dashboard.ts:92-93 (where: isAdmin ? {} : { type: { notIn: financeTypes } }); rendered for all users (dashboard-content.tsx:888, SSR-prefetched). (Verified first-hand.)
fix: Scope the feed to the viewer's visibility — exclude note activity for notes they cannot access (or strip titles) and filter project/task/client activity to their memberships.

summary: Leave requests can be self-approved and re-decided (no separation of duties)
preconditions: An HR (or admin) account that can submit a leave request.
steps: As HR, submit your own leave request (team.createLeaveRequest).
Call team.updateLeaveStatus({ id: <own>, status: 'APPROVED' }) — it succeeds.
Call it again on an already-APPROVED request to flip it to REJECTED.
expected: A reviewer cannot approve their OWN leave, and only PENDING requests are decidable (as resignation:review enforces).
actual: Only the coarse leave:approve capability (HR/ADMIN) is checked; no owner/PENDING resource conditions. The AI mirror setLeaveStatus filters PENDING but still lacks self-exclusion.
evidence: src/lib/abac/policies.ts:44 ('leave:approve': [isHrOrAdmin] — no attribute conditions); src/server/routers/team.ts:235-246; compare policies.ts:60-66.
fix: Load the request and reject if leave.userId === self or leave.status !== 'PENDING'; ideally add an attribute-conditioned leave:approve policy mirroring resignation:review.

role: Any user with EDIT on a SHARED note, or any user on a TEAM note
summary: Non-author editor can change a note's visibility (SHARED->TEAM exposure)
preconditions: User A owns a SHARED note shared with user B as EDIT (or any TEAM note).
steps: As B, call notes.update({ id, visibility: 'TEAM' }) — the note becomes visible company-wide.
Or set visibility: 'PRIVATE' to lock the author's other collaborators out.
Any user can do the same to a TEAM note (TEAM is editable by all).
expected: Visibility/sharing is the author's prerogative (setShares is author-only).
actual: update gates only on canEdit, which returns true for SHARED+EDIT grantees and anyone on a TEAM note, yet freely writes visibility (and projectId/clientId).
evidence: src/server/routers/notes.ts:71-76 (canEdit), :294-298; contrast author-only :368. AI mirror identical (src/lib/ai/tools/notes.ts:68-82, :357-359).
fix: Restrict visibility (and project/client re-attach) to note.authorId === userId (or ADMIN); editors get content/title only.

summary: Video-call attendance (logJoin) bypasses the anti-backfill window
preconditions: A recurring meeting (e.g. 09:00-09:30 standup) on which you are an attendee.
steps: At 02:00 (outside the live window) open /meetings/<id>/call.
The conference connects and fires videoConferenceJoined -> logJoin.
Observe an attendance log row stamps you 'present' for the resolved occurrence.
expected: markJoined refuses attendance outside [start-5min, end] to prevent retroactive attendance lies; the call path should too.
actual: logJoin — the primary, auto-fired attendance signal — has NO window check, so the strict and lax paths disagree and the lax one is the one users actually hit.
evidence: src/server/routers/meetings.ts:404-467 (logJoin, no guard) vs :261-271 (markJoined window check).
fix: Apply the same [start-5min, end] gate in logJoin (factor into a shared helper).

role: Channel member B removed by an admin/owner; A and B are employees
summary: No realtime revocation on channel removal — ex-member keeps live events
preconditions: Users A and B both members of private channel C; B has it open.
steps: An admin/owner calls removeMember({ channelId: C, userId: B }) (or B leaveChannels with the tab open).
A posts a message in C.
B's still-attached Ably subscription receives it and patches B's cache.
expected: Removal immediately cuts B off from live events.
actual: removeMember is a bare deleteMany with no emit; the Ably token capability is computed only at mint time with no short ttl; the client re-authorizes only when NEW channels appear, never on removal — so B keeps receiving live messages until a refetch + token renewal (default ~60 min) drops the subscription. History is correctly blocked by assertChannelMember, so this is a live-stream leak, not history.
fix: On removeMember/leaveChannel emit a user:{id} 'membership changed' event so the client refetches channels and calls client.auth.authorize() immediately; use a short token TTL.

summary: logLeave never fires on SPA nav/tab close -> attendance sessions stay open
preconditions: An in-progress meeting call you have joined.
steps: Join a call (logJoin stamps the row).
Leave by clicking another nav link in the app, or by closing/refreshing the tab (instead of the in-call hang-up).
Inspect the attendance log: leftAt is never written; the row stays open indefinitely.
expected: Every join gets a matching leftAt.
actual: logLeave is wired only to Jitsi's videoConferenceLeft/readyToClose; the effect cleanup only dispose()s the iframe and there is no beforeunload/pagehide/visibilitychange handler, so the common exit paths skew any duration/attendance-% math.
fix: Call logLeave in the effect cleanup and on pagehide/visibilitychange(hidden) (use navigator.sendBeacon/keepalive for unloads).

summary: Editing a message to add an @mention creates no notification
preconditions: A channel with at least two members.
steps: Send 'hello' in a channel.
Edit it to 'hello @Bob'.
Observe Bob's mention row and highlight are created, but he gets no bell/notification.
expected: sendMessage fires notify() + emitToUser for new mentions; editMessage should too.
actual: editMessage recomputes and persists validMentions but never calls notify/emitToUser, so mentions introduced by an edit are silently un-notified.
evidence: src/server/routers/chat.ts:341-397 (no notify/emitToUser after the edit transaction).
fix: Diff new mentions against the pre-edit set and notify the newly-added ones (guard against re-notifying existing mentions).

role: Any DM participant; then any party with the URL (incl. unauthenticated)
summary: Uploaded files (incl. private-DM voice/attachments) world-readable by URL
preconditions: A private DM in which you can send an attachment/voice message.
steps: Send a voice message/attachment in a private DM.
Note the returned URL /uploads/<uuid>-<name>.
Fetch that URL with no authentication (or as a removed member) — the file bytes are served.
expected: File bytes are gated by channel membership like the message content.
actual: Files land at public/uploads/<uuid>-<name>, served statically with no auth. The UUID prefix prevents enumeration but not post-disclosure access (a removed member, a referer/log leak, link sharing). The MIME+extension allowlist is solid against stored-XSS (.html/.svg excluded).
evidence: src/app/api/upload/route.ts:80-89 writes to public/uploads and returns /uploads/...; public/uploads/ exists and is statically served. (Verified first-hand.)
fix: Serve attachments through an authenticated route that re-checks assertChannelMember, or use signed short-lived URLs (Vercel Blob with token). Severity depends on deployment (prod uses public storage).

role: Any (unauthenticated for login; any token for REST)
summary: No rate limiting anywhere (REST API and login)
preconditions: Network access to the app.
steps: Call any /api/v1 endpoint, or the NextAuth login authorize, in an unbounded loop.
Flood with invalid df_ tokens.
Observe no throttling / no 429.
expected: Per-token/per-IP limits returning 429; capped login attempts.
actual: None exist (repo-wide grep for rate.?limit|throttle|upstash|429 returns nothing; proxy.ts:14-22 short-circuits /api/v1 with no limiting). Each auth attempt runs a bcrypt compare per prefix-matching candidate, so unthrottled floods are CPU-amplifying.
evidence: src/proxy.ts:14-22; src/lib/api-auth.ts:55-57; src/lib/auth.ts:89. (Verified first-hand: grep returns nothing.)
fix: Add per-token + per-IP rate limiting (edge middleware / Upstash), and cap login + auth attempts.

summary: order treated as contiguous index; Trello import writes gapped orders
preconditions: A board imported from Trello whose cards interleave across lists.
steps: Import a Trello board whose cards are distributed across multiple lists.
In an imported column, drag a task one slot down.
Observe the move silently no-ops or misorders.
expected: Per-column order is 0..n and a one-slot move works.
actual: Import assigns a GLOBAL running counter as each task's order, so a column can have orders like [2,5,9]. moveTask then does range math (order: { gte: newOrder, lt: oldOrder }) assuming newOrder (a client array index) is comparable to stored order — gte:1, lt:2 matches nothing, so the task doesn't move.
fix: Normalize order per-column on import (0..n); have moveTask recompute positions from the actual ordered list rather than trusting client indices.

summary: Deleting a column silently cascade-deletes all its tasks (no count/warning)
preconditions: A column containing tasks (with comments/checklists/attachments).
steps: Click the trash icon on a column with tasks.
Confirm via the tiny inline 'Delete / No'.
Observe all tasks (and their comments/checklists/attachments) are permanently destroyed.
expected: A warning naming the task count, or a move-first flow.
actual: Task.column is onDelete: Cascade and the UI shows no count; the only hint is the card-count badge.
fix: Block deletion of non-empty columns, or show 'This will delete X tasks' and require explicit confirmation.

summary: Task attachments are fetched but never rendered, and cannot be added
preconditions: A task that has attachments (e.g. imported from Trello).
steps: Open a task whose card shows a paperclip attachment count.
Open the task detail sheet.
Observe there is no attachments section, and no way to add an attachment.
expected: Attachments are visible/openable, and can be added/removed.
actual: getTaskDetail includes attachments but task-detail-sheet.tsx never references them, and there is no addTaskAttachment/deleteTaskAttachment mutation anywhere — the data is invisible and unreachable.
evidence: getTaskDetail includes attachments at src/server/routers/projects.ts:885; task-detail-sheet.tsx renders labels/assignees/checklists/comments but not attachments.
fix: Render an Attachments section and add upload/delete mutations (reuse the /api/upload pipeline).

summary: createTask/updateTaskAssignees accept arbitrary user IDs
preconditions: A project you can access.
steps: Call createTask/updateTaskAssignees with a userId that is not a project member.
Or pass a userId that does not exist.
expected: Rejected (setColumnDefaultAssignees validates membership).
actual: createTask and updateTaskAssignees do not validate membership; a non-member is assigned and emailed about a project they aren't on, and an invalid ID raises a raw Prisma FK 500. updateTaskAssignees uses createMany with no skipDuplicates/validation, so a dup/invalid ID throws.
evidence: setColumnDefaultAssignees validates membership (src/server/routers/projects.ts:457-470); createTask (:529-541) and updateTaskAssignees (:950-955) do not.
fix: Validate assigneeIds against ProjectMember (mirroring setColumnDefaultAssignees) before create.

summary: Deleting a client with invoices fails with a raw FK error
preconditions: A client that has at least one invoice.
steps: As admin, open a client that has >=1 invoice.
Click Delete and confirm.
Observe the page fails with a generic error.
expected: A clean 'Cannot delete: client has invoices', or a defined cascade.
actual: Invoice.clientId is a required relation with NO onDelete (Prisma default = Restrict; contrast contacts/contracts/transactions which are explicit Cascade), so the delete throws P2003 surfaced as a generic error; the UI renders no deleteClient.error.
fix: Pre-count invoices and return a friendly BAD_REQUEST (or define an explicit referential action); surface the error in the UI.

summary: resetMemberPassword ships a Groq-incompatible pattern/allOf schema
preconditions: An admin assistant session that routes to the people tool domain.
steps: Admin asks the assistant: 'reset Aisha's password to Hunter2024'.
The people domain loads; resetMemberPassword is offered to Groq with newPassword: passwordSchema.
Observe (if Groq rejects pattern/allOf like it does format) the entire request 400s.
expected: No format/pattern/allOf in schemas sent to Groq (the project's own convention — inviteMember and client-website tools drop .email()/.url() and validate in execute).
actual: passwordSchema (z.string().min(8).regex().regex().regex()) serializes to allOf:[{pattern:...},{pattern:...},{pattern:...}]. If Groq rejects pattern/allOf, the WHOLE request 400s, breaking every admin turn that loads the people domain (lay-off, hire, role change, leave approval) — and approval-continuations force the full toolset, so potentially any admin-approved write.
evidence: src/lib/ai/tools/people.ts:940 (newPassword: passwordSchema); src/lib/password-policy.ts:21-26; contrast people.ts:722-737; force-full-toolset src/app/api/assistant/route.ts:64.
fix: Use newPassword: z.string().min(8) and call the exported passwordMeetsPolicy() inside execute. (Confidence Medium: pattern emission confirmed; the 400 outcome depends on Groq — verify with one admin people-domain request.)

summary: Password change does not revoke other active sessions
preconditions: The same account signed in on two devices.
steps: Sign in on device 1 and device 2.
Change your password on device 1 (team.changePassword).
Observe device 2's session keeps working for up to the 8h token lifetime.
expected: A password change invalidates other sessions.
actual: The JWT revalidation re-reads only role/status/department/title, never a password epoch, so pre-change stateless tokens stay valid.
fix: Add passwordChangedAt/tokenVersion to User, stamp it into the JWT at sign-in, compare on each jwt() refresh and force logout on mismatch (also enables force-logout on lay-off/reset). (Confidence Medium — inherent to JWT, but fixable.)

summary: /api/v1/spec bypasses withApiAuth and is never audited
preconditions: Any valid token.
steps: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer df_<any>' https://<host>/api/v1/spec
Inspect the audit log — neither the read of the full API map nor 401 attempts on this path appear.
expected: Every /api/v1 path is audited, including auth failures.
actual: The route calls authenticateApiRequest directly with no recordRestAudit, so reads of the full API map and 401 attempts leave no audit trail (405s on other routes are similarly unaudited).
fix: Wrap with withApiAuth or call recordRestAudit manually for both success and the auth-fail early return.

role: df_ token with a write scope
summary: Malformed JSON body -> 500 instead of 400 (all writes)
preconditions: A token with a write scope.
steps: curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer df_<tasks-write>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-raw 'not-json' https://<host>/api/v1/tasks
expected: 400 Bad Request.
actual: await request.json() throws before Zod and is caught as a generic 500 (no leak, wrong status, pollutes 500 metrics/audit). Affects every write handler.
evidence: e.g. src/app/api/v1/tasks/route.ts:53 with the catch at src/lib/api-auth.ts:171-184.
fix: Wrap request.json() in a shared parseJson helper returning 400 on SyntaxError.

role: df_ token with a read scope
summary: Non-numeric ?limit= -> 500 on /tasks & /transactions GET
preconditions: A token with tasks:read or finance:read.
steps: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer df_<tasks-read>' 'https://<host>/api/v1/tasks?limit=abc'
expected: A clamped default.
actual: parseInt('abc')->NaN, Math.min(NaN,100)->NaN, take:NaN -> Prisma validation error -> caught -> 500. clients/projects/invoices/meetings already clamp safely; tasks & transactions use the old pattern.
fix: Apply parseInt(x,10) || <default> + Math.max(...,1) clamp used in the standardized routes.

role: df_ token with a write scope
summary: Unvalidated foreign keys -> 500 instead of 400/404
preconditions: A token with a write scope and a valid columnId.
steps: curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer df_<tasks-write>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"title":"x","columnId":"<valid>","assigneeIds":["does-not-exist"]}' https://<host>/api/v1/tasks
expected: A clean 400/404.
actual: Bad/nonexistent related IDs (assigneeIds/labelIds on tasks; attendeeIds on meetings; projectId/clientId on transactions/invoices) are inserted without existence checks, causing a Prisma FK violation -> generic 500. Tasks can also be assigned to non-members.
fix: Validate referenced IDs exist (and assignees are project members) before insert; return 400/404.

summary: Profit/margin computed with JS float arithmetic on Decimals
preconditions: Finance data where income/expense have fractional parts.
steps: Set income 1000.10 and expense 999.90.
Read the raw API/AI JSON profit/margin (not the toLocaleString UI).
expected: profit 0.20.
actual: Sums are exact Decimal, but Number(_sum)-Number(_sum) and (income-expense)/income*100 run in JS float, giving 0.20000000000000018; margin compounds it. Masked by toLocaleString in the UI but leaks in raw API/AI JSON.
fix: Do subtraction/margin in Prisma.Decimal (or integer cents) before the final Number().

summary: P&L month-end drops final 999 ms; invoice-number race + cross-year reset
preconditions: Concurrent invoice creation; a transaction at 23:59:59.5xx on month-end.
steps: Create a transaction dated 2026-05-31 23:59:59.500 and view the P&L month bucket.
Create two invoices concurrently and observe a possible duplicate invoice number; create the first invoice of a new year and observe it is not -001.
expected: Month-end inclusive to the ms; unique sequential per-year invoice numbers.
actual: P&L endOfMonth uses ...59,59 (no ms), dropping a 23:59:59.5 row. INV-${year}-${count+1} from a non-transactional global count() can produce duplicate numbers under concurrency and never resets to -001 in a new year (count is across all years).
fix: Use ...59,999 and an atomic per-year sequence/counter for invoice numbers.

summary: adminUpdateMember has no last-admin guard -> admin lockout
preconditions: You are the only remaining active ADMIN.
steps: Call team.adminUpdateMember({ id: <self or last admin>, role: 'EMPLOYEE' }) — or { status: 'INACTIVE' }.
Observe it succeeds, leaving the workspace with zero active admins.
expected: The same last-active-admin guard layOffMember enforces.
actual: Admin-only, so not escalation/IDOR — an availability/consistency gap: adminUpdateMember applies the Zod input straight to user.update with no admin-count check. The guard exists in layOffMember and the AI updateMember tool, but not here.
fix: Mirror the layOffMember last-admin check whenever role moves away from ADMIN or status becomes INACTIVE.

summary: Client-directory trust boundary inconsistent across tRPC/REST/AI
preconditions: An employee web session and a REST token.
steps: As an employee, call trpc clients.getAll / search — full client directory (name/industry/location/status) is returned.
Via REST, GET /api/v1/clients as a non-admin token — 403.
Via the assistant, listClients (non-admin) is project-scoped but globalSearch shows all client names.
expected: One consistent policy for who may enumerate clients.
actual: REST treats clients as admin-only (clients/[id]/route.ts:10), tRPC exposes the directory to every employee (clients.ts:16-44, search.ts:72-77), and the AI scopes non-admins to project-reachable clients but globalSearch shows all names. The three surfaces disagree.
fix: Pick one policy and apply uniformly (likely align tRPC/search with the assistant's project-scoped visibility, or relax the REST gate).

summary: Attendance create is non-atomic -> concurrent double-join throws P2002 (500)
preconditions: Two near-simultaneous joins for the same (meeting,user,occurrence) — e.g. StrictMode double-invoke, or markJoined firing alongside logJoin.
steps: Trigger two concurrent joins for the same occurrence.
Observe the second create hits the unique constraint and throws an unhandled P2002 (500).
expected: Double-join is a no-op (as the comment claims).
actual: The code does findUnique-then-create (not upsert), so a genuine race surfaces a 500 instead of a no-op.
fix: Use a real upsert on the meetingId_userId_occurrenceStart unique key, or wrap create in a try/catch that swallows P2002.

summary: Client timeline sorts by createdAt only (no id tiebreak) — unstable order
preconditions: Multiple messages created within the same millisecond (e.g. a burst).
steps: Send several messages rapidly so some share a createdAt millisecond.
Observe client order may not match the server and can reshuffle across re-renders.
expected: Client order mirrors the server's stable [createdAt desc, id desc].
actual: The client re-sort uses only new Date(a.createdAt)-new Date(b.createdAt); same-ms messages are unstable.
evidence: Server: src/server/routers/chat.ts:102 ([createdAt desc, id desc]); client: src/components/chat/message/message-list.tsx:64-66.
fix: Add an id tiebreak to the client comparator to mirror the server.

summary: markRead broadcasts every member's lastReadAt to the whole channel
preconditions: A channel you are a member of and an Ably subscription.
steps: Subscribe to channel:<id> via a custom Ably client.
Observe each member's lastReadAt read-receipt event is delivered to the whole channel.
expected: Per-user read state stays private (the client only acts on its own).
actual: markRead emits each user's lastReadAt to channel:{id}; anyone subscribed can observe everyone's read times even though onRead returns for who !== myId.
fix: If per-user read state isn't a product feature, emit read updates to the actor's own user:{id} channel instead of the shared channel.

summary: Recurring-meeting list shows the next (empty) occurrence, hiding attendance
preconditions: A recurring meeting viewed in the latter half of the gap between occurrences.
steps: View the meetings list when 'now' is closer to the next occurrence than to the previous one's end.
Observe the just-finished occurrence's attendance disappears from the list before the next meeting starts.
expected: Attendance for the most recent past occurrence remains until the next actually starts.
actual: findRelevantOccurrence picks the nearest occurrence, so in the latter half of a gap the list shows the next (empty) occurrence and the prior occurrence's attendance disappears early.
fix: For attendance display, prefer the most recent past occurrence until the next one actually starts.

summary: addComment does not verify parentId belongs to the same task
preconditions: A task you can access and a comment id from a different task.
steps: Call addComment with a taskId you can access but a parentId of a comment on a different task/project.
Observe a reply row is created threaded under the foreign comment.
expected: Rejected when parent.taskId !== input.taskId.
actual: Only assertTaskAccess(taskId) runs; parentId is passed straight through, creating an orphaned reply that pollutes data.
fix: Look up the parent and assert parent.taskId === input.taskId.

summary: Task-completion logged only for a column named exactly 'Done'
preconditions: A board whose final column is not literally named 'Done' (e.g. 'Shipped', or an imported 'Complete' list).
steps: Rename the final column to 'Shipped' (or import a Trello board with a 'Complete' list).
Move a task into it.
Observe no task_completed activity is recorded.
expected: Completion is recorded for the final/done column.
actual: The check is an exact case-sensitive string match (name === 'Done'), while the board preview uses a DONE_RE regex — inconsistent.
fix: Use the same done-detection heuristic (regex / last-column) as the UI, or a per-column 'is done' flag.

summary: Contracts/projects/milestones accept endDate before startDate
preconditions: Admin creating/editing a contract.
steps: Create/edit a contract with Start = 2026-12-01 and End = 2026-01-01.
Observe it saves and the list renders 'Dec 1, 2026 - Jan 1, 2026'.
expected: A validation error.
actual: No cross-field .refine on contracts, projects, or milestones; the inverted range is saved as-is.
fix: Add a Zod .refine(d => !d.startDate || !d.endDate || d.endDate >= d.startDate).

summary: Contract signedAt auto-stamp inconsistent (status dropdown vs edit form)
preconditions: A DRAFT contract.
steps: Edit a DRAFT contract, set Status = SIGNED via the edit form (leave Signed Date blank), save.
Observe signedAt is NOT stamped (the inline status dropdown does stamp it).
expected: signedAt is stamped on first SIGNED, like the inline status dropdown does.
actual: setContractStatus stamps signedAt; updateContract writes the raw payload only and never sets signedAt.
fix: Apply the same stamp-on-first-SIGNED logic in updateContract.

summary: Malformed date strings in a Trello export crash the whole import
preconditions: A Trello JSON export where a card 'due' or a comment 'date' is a non-parseable string.
steps: Import a Trello JSON with an invalid date string.
Observe the entire transactional import fails with a generic 'Internal server error'.
expected: The card imports with a null/skipped date.
actual: new Date(badString) -> Invalid Date -> the whole transactional import fails; the schema only constrains these to string, not a valid datetime.
fix: Guard with const d = new Date(x); isNaN(d.getTime()) ? null : d (and skip/clamp invalid comment dates).

summary: addContact skips email validation; no contact edit/delete UI at all
preconditions: A client.
steps: Call addContact with email='not-an-email' — it is accepted (create enforces .email()).
After creating a contact, try to edit or remove it in the UI — there is no control.
expected: Consistent email validation; full contact CRUD UI.
actual: addContact uses email: z.string().optional() while create uses .email() — inconsistent. addContact/deleteContact exist but have no UI (the Contacts tab only lists), and there is no updateContact mutation at all.
fix: Align email validation; add contact CRUD UI + an updateContact mutation.

summary: Client create/edit forms swallow validation errors (no feedback)
preconditions: A client create/edit form.
steps: Enter a website not starting with http(s):// and submit.
Observe the mutation fails server-side but the form shows no error and just sits there.
expected: The validation error is shown inline (as the Projects forms do).
actual: optionalWebsiteUrl rejects non-http(s) values but neither CreateClientForm nor the edit card renders createClient.error/updateClient.error.
fix: Render the mutation error inline.

summary: Leave requests accept invalid/overlapping/past date ranges
preconditions: Any active employee.
steps: Call team.createLeaveRequest({ type:'VACATION', startDate: 2026-07-10, endDate: 2026-07-01 }) — succeeds (end before start).
Submit past-dated and fully-overlapping duplicate requests — also accepted.
expected: endDate >= startDate; reject past ranges; ideally block overlaps / check a balance.
actual: Input is passed straight to create with no cross-field checks, corrupting the HR 'out today' and team-stats math.
fix: Add a Zod .refine(endDate >= startDate), reject startDate < today, and query overlapping requests of the same user/status.

summary: getStats returns company-wide pending-leave count to non-admins
preconditions: An employee session.
steps: As an employee, call dashboard.getStats.
Observe pendingLeaves is the unfiltered company-wide count, even though the card only renders for admins.
expected: pendingLeaves is gated/scoped server-side (like the revenue block).
actual: pendingLeaves is computed unconditionally and shipped to every client; the AI getDashboardStats mirrors this, and getTeamMember returns any colleague's full project-membership list.
fix: Compute pendingLeaves only when isAdmin (or scope to the requester), like the revenue/expenses block.

summary: Edge middleware authorizes on cookie presence only (no signature check)
preconditions: Ability to send an arbitrary Cookie header.
steps: Send a request with header Cookie: authjs.session-token=anything.
Observe proxy.ts lets it through the edge gate without verifying the JWT (real enforcement is downstream in auth()/tRPC).
expected: The middleware treats unverified cookies as unauthenticated.
actual: It only substring-matches the cookie name; a forged/expired cookie passes the edge gate but is rejected at the data layer. It also does no role-based route protection (those rely on per-page redirect()). pathname.includes('.') also treats any dotted path as a static asset.
fix: Verify the token with NextAuth getToken/auth in middleware rather than substring-matching the cookie. (Defense-in-depth; not a direct data leak — downstream guards hold.)

summary: CSP connect-src ends with ws: wss: wildcards + stale localhost:3001
preconditions: None (inspect response headers).
steps: Request any page and inspect the Content-Security-Policy header's connect-src.
Observe it ends with blanket 'ws: wss:' and includes the stale socketOrigin.
expected: Websockets restricted to the explicit Ably/8x8 hosts.
actual: The trailing 'ws: wss:' allows a WebSocket to ANY host, nullifying the scoped Ably/8x8 allowlist above it; socketOrigin (NEXT_PUBLIC_SOCKET_URL) is the stale Socket.IO origin (live header showed http://localhost:3001).
evidence: next.config.ts:33. (Verified first-hand via live response header.)
fix: Drop 'ws: wss:' and the dead socket origin; rely on the explicit ablyOrigins/jaasConnect entries.

summary: img-src 'self' data: https: allows images from any HTTPS origin
preconditions: None.
steps: Inspect the CSP img-src directive.
Observe any https image URL is loadable.
expected: Images restricted to the app origin + known avatar hosts.
actual: img-src permits images from any origin (tracking-pixel/exfil surface), laxer than the next/image host lock-down.
fix: Restrict img-src to the app origin + known avatar hosts.

summary: Inconsistent page-level auth — most pages rely on proxy+tRPC, not auth()
preconditions: A stale/invalid but present session cookie.
steps: With a stale/forged session cookie, navigate to /dashboard (and most non-admin pages).
Observe the page shell renders and tRPC prefetches fail UNAUTHORIZED — a broken/empty page instead of a clean login redirect.
expected: Consistent server-side page auth — a clean redirect to /login.
actual: finance/audit-logs/team-stats/hr hard-gate via auth()+redirect, but /dashboard and most pages rely on the proxy cookie-presence check + tRPC, so a stale cookie lands on a broken shell. No data leak (tRPC enforces), but inconsistent UX.
fix: Add a shared server-side page-auth guard so non-finance pages also redirect cleanly on no/invalid session.

summary: Assistant eval never exercises execute-level guards or resource isolation
preconditions: Review of scripts/assistant-eval.ts.
steps: Read the employee/HR security cases: tools are built with that role's context, so privileged tools aren't even constructed.
Note the forbid/mustNotInclude assertions pass vacuously; no cross-user IDOR case exists.
expected: At least one case proving an admin-gated tool refuses when its execute is reached in a non-admin context, and note/DM/meeting isolation cases.
actual: Only routing and 'not offered' are gated; the in-execute if(!h.isAdmin) return {error} checks are never tested, and resetMemberPassword's schema path (AI-01) is unexercised.
fix: Add cases that invoke an admin tool's execute under an employee subject (expect {error}), read a PRIVATE/SHARED note and a non-member channel as an employee (expect no leak), and load resetMemberPassword.

summary: getDashboardStats.pendingLeaves + getTeamMember over-share (tRPC parity)
preconditions: An employee assistant session.
steps: Ask the assistant for dashboard stats — pendingLeaves is the company-wide PENDING count.
Ask about a colleague — getTeamMember returns their complete projectMembers list.
expected: Employee figures are their own / scoped; colleague project membership is scoped.
actual: pendingLeaves counts all PENDING company-wide for every role; getTeamMember returns the target's complete projectMembers list to any viewer. Both faithfully mirror the tRPC surfaces (dashboard.getStats:33-35, team.getById:175-177) — a pre-existing app-wide behavior, NOT an assistant-specific escalation.
fix: If undesired, scope pendingLeaves to isAdminOrHr (else self) and the returned project list to the viewer's own projects — fixing router and tool together to keep parity.

summary: Approval is a UX confirmation, not the security boundary (record-only)
preconditions: Understanding of the approval flow.
steps: Note the client supplies the full messages history including tool-approval-response parts.
A crafted request could forge/replay an approved:true part with a matching approvalId.
expected: The approval gate is not relied upon as the authorization boundary.
actual: Not exploitable for escalation — every write execute independently re-checks authorization (h.isAdmin/h.can/object guards) and all writes set needsApproval:true. A forged approval can at most let the acting user skip their own confirmation for an action they are already entitled to perform; fabricated tool results yield fake (not real) data. Recorded so the in-execute authz is never relaxed.
fix: Keep the in-execute authorization checks authoritative; never relax them on the assumption the approval gate protects them.
